There are different factors to consider when buying shares. Some of these factors include: the level of risk associated with buying shares, understanding the economic climate, knowledge of the share industry and price to earnings ratio (P/E ratio). You are going to investigate the price to earnings ratio of different shares and determine the best share to buy.

Explain what the P/E ratio is in your own words?

notes: Standard 2 paper, William Clarke College AT1 (assessed 18/11/2020, Term 4 of Year 11, so year taken as the 2021 graduation year). Total 38 = Section I 11 + Section II 16 + Section III 11. Paper typos: the Section II header says 'Attempt Questions 7-8' but contains only Q6; the Section III header says 'Attempt Question 6' but contains only Q7; Q6(c) refers to 'Kerrie's car' though the car is the Hyundai i30 bought by 'you'. Q1 is preceded by an intro paragraph that applies to Questions 1-4; it is kept in Q1 only. Q6(d) is stored as a parent part with unmarked intro text and sub-parts (i) and (ii) of 1 mark each. Question-paper mark labels ([n marks]) are stored in marks, not in the text. Solution typos: Q6a guideline gives depreciation $1638.40 = $1637 (should round to $1638); Q6b guideline labels 0.8^7 = 0.209 and 0.8^8 = 0.262 (0.262 is actually 0.8^6; answer 7 years stands); Q7d guideline mark column shows 1 but paper allocates 2 marks to part (d) (Section III totals 11 only with 2). Q7 statement table and Q6(c) grid are cropped as figures; Q2 and Q6 depreciation tables are stored as tables data with blank cells to fill. The Q3 solution graph is cropped from page 9.
